contract.direct_answer:
DESIGN PROPOSAL (ranked candidate set — NOT a validated result; routes through causal-pruner + human gate before any wet-lab commitment).

Goal: test SUFFICIENCY of a pronephric program — i.e. whether forcing a candidate transcription-factor (TF) module is ENOUGH to induce/expand pronephric fate in non-pronephric or naive tissue.

--- MINIMAL PERTURBATION SET (gain-of-function, ranked) ---
The evidence bundle names candidate pronephros/kidney-relevant TFs only in the RN2 niche description (pax2a, wt1a, plus tfap2a/foxc1a which are more eye/neural-crest associated). No ENSDARG identifiers were verified in this bundle, so I do NOT assert IDs.

Rank 1 (single-factor): Ectopic/heat-shock or mRNA overexpression of pax2a alone. Rationale: pax2a is the strongest listed pronephros-associated TF; a single-factor GOF is the most interpretable sufficiency test.
Rank 2 (single-factor): wt1a alone (intermediate mesoderm / podocyte-associated).
Rank 3 (combinatorial): pax2a + wt1a co-expression — tests whether a two-factor module is sufficient when neither is alone, addressing partial-sufficiency.
(A dose/timing arm — inducible hsp70-driven expression at staged timepoints across the 3–24 hpf window covered by ZESTA/CORPUS-2026-0001 — should be nested within each rank.)

Readout: induction of pronephric markers (e.g. pax2a/wt1a targets and tubule/duct markers) by in situ / spatial transcriptomics (ZESTA-type Stereo-seq) in ectopic domains.

--- REQUIRED CONTROLS ---
1. Vehicle / empty-construct or mismatched-mRNA control (injection/heat-shock trauma control).
2. Non-inducible line + heat-shock (heat-shock toxicity control).
3. Inducible line WITHOUT heat-shock (leaky-expression control).
4. Positive control: a domain that normally expresses the factor (confirms construct is functional).
5. Marker-specificity control: an unrelated lineage marker to show induction is pronephros-specific, not global mesendoderm.
6. Dose ladder (low→high mRNA/construct) to separate true sufficiency from overexpression artifact.

--- POSSIBLE CONFOUNDERS ---
- Competence window: the receiving tissue may only respond within a narrow stage → apparent "insufficiency" is really a timing effect.
- Endogenous co-factors: pax2a/wt1a may require partners (RA signaling, Notch/Jagged per RN2) present only in intermediate mesoderm → "sufficiency" may be context-dependent, not intrinsic.
- Overexpression toxicity / off-target activation of paralogs (pax2b, wt1b) — paralog cross-talk not resolvable from this bundle.
- Marker ambiguity: pax2a is also expressed in midbrain-hindbrain boundary/otic/eye → ectopic pax2a signal ≠ pronephric fate. Must use downstream tubule identity markers, not the driver itself.
- Secondary (non-cell-autonomous) induction vs. direct fate conversion — needs clonal/mosaic labeling to distinguish.

CAUSAL-PRUNER + HUMAN GATE: candidate ranking above is heuristic; the pruner should test for confounded edges (RA/Notch co-requirement) and a human must approve factor IDs against the verified Ensembl store before execution.
alternatives_considered: Loss-of-function (CRISPR/morpholino) design instead of GOF — rejected because sufficiency (not necessity) was the explicit question; LOF tests necessity.
Larger combinatorial factor screen (add lhx1a, hnf1b, osr1) — not proposed because none of these are named in the evidence bundle and I cannot assert them from memory.
Using the anterior-segment/cornea atlas (CORPUS-2026-0002) as the readout platform — rejected; it is an eye-focused dataset, not pronephric.
